Action Plan:
1. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
2. Advise trigger avoidance and protective measures:
   - Wear gloves at all times when cleaning to reduce exposure to cleaning products.
   - Minimize contact with irritants; correlate symptoms with hotel cleaning duties and recent job change.
3. Initiate skin-directed therapy for inflammation and dryness:
   - Start topical corticosteroid cream for palmar inflammation (name/strength not documented in transcript; dose/route/frequency not documented).
   - Initiate stronger emollients to coat the hands 3–4 times daily for the next 2 weeks.
   - Continue avoidance of irritants and use of emollients; discontinue or limit ineffective OTC products (OTC moisturizers previously tried without relief; antihistamines tried without relief).
4. Monitoring and follow-up:
   - If improving, continue therapy for about 1–2 weeks; reassess at that time.
   - If no improvement or if spreading/worsening occurs, return sooner for re-evaluation and possible additional treatment.
5. Medication procurement:
   - Prescription for topical steroid and stronger emollients will be sent to the patient’s pharmacy (dose/route/frequency not documented).
6. Additional notes:
   - “A COVID-19 vaccine suitability assessment was performed” is not applicable based on the transcript; no vaccine update provided.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness and cracking of skin on the hands, predominantly the palms; very dry.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms started about 3–4 months ago; gradually worsened and now painful enough to affect work.
- Location: Palms primarily; milder dryness on legs.
- Itching: Yes, intermittent.
- Bleeding: Occasional bleeding with scratching; not spontaneous.
- Aggravating/relieving factors: Likely related to cleaning products used at work; inconsistent glove use; recently changed job (4 months ago).
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus on metformin.
- Medications: Metformin.
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Hotel housekeeper; sometimes does not wear gloves; non-smoker; alcohol: a couple of pints per week.
- Family history: Diabetes noted in family.
- Review of systems: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms; appetite normal; feels generally well otherwise.

Objective:
- General: No systemic symptoms reported.
- Skin and mucous membranes: Palms very cracked, dry, and itchy; scratching occasionally causes bleeding. No mention of systemic signs or other body areas affected.
- Other: Leg dryness reported but milder; no other notable exam findings described.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Issue: Dermatitis/hand dermatitis, likely irritant contact dermatitis
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis (high likelihood)
   - Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):
     - Allergic contact dermatitis (medium-high likelihood): plausible given exposure to cleaning agents; consider patch testing if not improving.
     - Hand dermatitis/eczema (medium likelihood): fits chronic dry, itchy hands with fissures.
     - Xerosis with diabetes/metabolic dryness (medium-low likelihood): diabetes can predispose to dry skin, but palmar fissuring with itching favors dermatitis.
   - Investigations planned: None at this time.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Dermatitis management with protective gloves during cleaning; reduce irritant exposure.
     - Topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation (name/strength not documented; route/dose/frequency not documented).
     - Stronger emollients, applied to the hands 3–4 times daily for about 2 weeks.
   - Referrals: None at this time.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: No vitals recorded; no specific medication names/doses documented for the topical steroid or emollients; no allergy history update beyond “no allergies” already captured.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear narrative; minor repetition, but enough detail to support assessment and plan.
